title.narrative: Coherent Policies generate inclusive job-rich growth, promotes skill and capacity development and employment generation

description.narrative: In Liberia’s North-Central Region, human insecurity is multi-faceted, complex and deeply rooted. Despite abundant natural resources, socio-economic insecurity remains a major concern. Food and social insecurity—especially for women and children—are linked to land disputes, limited economic opportunities, poor infrastructure, and low income. The region’s counties—Bong, Lofa, and Nimba—have endured three major crises: prolonged civil conflict, the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, and the COVID-19 pandemic. These events severely disrupted social and economic life, causing widespread poverty, unemployment, food insecurity, and environmental degradation, all amid weak or non-existent social protection systems. The civil war, which lasted nearly two decades, had its most devastating impact on these three counties, now home to several concession companies. The Ebola outbreak further strained the region, with Bong, Lofa, and Nimba recording the highest death tolls. Consequently, poverty, unemployment, environmental degradation, food insecurity, pockets of conflicts exist in the region amidst weak/non-existent social protection. This intervention aims to address the region’s interconnected human security challenges—particularly food, social, and economic insecurity—at the community level. It will serve as a model for human security through “protection” and “empowerment” strategies. The initiative targets 3,000 vulnerable young women and men, including youth with disabilities, ensuring gender balance (50% male, 50% female). An additional 10,000 individuals will benefit indirectly, with 2,500 of them specifically targeted to maintain gender parity across all outcomes, outputs, and activities. The goal is to build resilience and promote inclusive development in one of Liberia’s most affected regions.
